title: Opening of the Suez Canal
summary: On 17 November 1869, the Suez Canal was officially opened to international navigation, linking the Mediterranean Sea directly to the Red Sea across the Isthmus of Suez in Egypt. Built under Ferdinand de Lesseps over ten years of construction, the sea-level waterway eliminated the lengthy voyage around Africa's Cape of Good Hope, drastically reducing maritime transit times between Europe and Asia and reshaping global trade networks and geopolitics.

uncertainty.note: Official inauguration took place on 17 November 1869 with an inaugural procession of ships entering the canal.

as_recorded.value: LE . 17 . NOVEMBRE . 1869 . LE . CANAL . MARITIME . A . ETE . OUVERT . A . LA . GRANDE . NAVIGATION (On 17 November 1869 the sea canal was opened for grand navigation)
In 1869, after 10 years of work by the French, the Suez Canal joined the Mediterranean and Red Seas.

importance.justification: The Suez Canal fundamentally shortened maritime routes between Europe and Asia, revolutionizing international shipping and transforming global trade infrastructure.
